ov: The Atlantic sturgeon, a big bottom-feeding fish armoured with five rows of bony plates instead of true scales. It lives along the coast of eastern North America and swims up rivers to spawn. Once abundant, it was overfished for caviar and is now threatened in much of its range.

why.et: Fished above all for caviar made from its eggs, and for its flesh; 19th-century overharvesting caused its collapse.

wt: Usually under 140 kg; up to over 360 kg
rg: Eastern North America, from New Brunswick in Canada to Florida, plus a reintroduced population in the Baltic Sea region of Europe.
df: Crustaceans, worms and molluscs from the bottom.
fx: It sometimes leaps completely out of the water, and nobody knows exactly why.
Only 22 of its 38 original spawning rivers still have viable populations.
